title: Rails, Rack::Deflater
notes: The generated Rails application with Rack::Deflater added, so responses are gzipped. It stands in for the compressing proxy that a generated deployment puts in front.
details: The Rails entry with one change: Rack::Deflater is put in front of the middleware stack (config.middleware.insert_before ActionDispatch::Static, Rack::Deflater in an initializer), so every response is gzip-compressed inside the measured process for a client that accepts it. A generated application leaves compression to Thruster, a proxy in a second process that this benchmark does not run; this is the same work done in the one process, to compare with frameworks that compress by default. Everything else is the Rails entry, and its notes apply. Gems are installed one at a time from gems.lock.json after their age and sha256 are checked, and loaded through Bundler with a frozen Gemfile.lock; seven of them (bigdecimal, bootsnap, msgpack, nio4r, puma, racc, websocket-driver) compile native extensions at install.
